tasks.short: Learn material and pass certification tests.

steps.what: Learn the material for the certification.
File the certificate the dispatcher already passed.

tasks.design: The dispatcher learns the material and passes the required tests. A file copy of a certificate they have already passed can be stored. The test is not taken by a tool, and the learning is not shortened by a summary.
tasks.previous_blocker: The course and the test were already a person's work. The certificate was then copied into a folder.
tasks.enabler_now: A passed certificate can be filed once. That does not change the test.
tasks.still_hard: The test is invigilated, and the material has to be learned by the person who will take calls.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher learns and passes. A filed certificate is not the qualification.
tasks.altitude: Learning and the test stay. Filing a certificate that was already passed is a little shorter.

reach.task: Check that a dispatcher is certified
reach.learn: Treat the certificate as filed only after the person has passed

evidence.claim: A certificate the person has already passed can be filed. The test itself stays with the person.

assumptions: The workflow starts when the dispatcher begins the material and ends when a passed certificate is filed. The test stays in person.
The file is the certificate identifier and the date. The dispatcher produces the pass by sitting the test. No practice score is stored as a trait.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree.
Upkeep is small: the file uses the certificate the examiner already issued.
unknowns: Who issues the certificate, and whether a paper original must be kept.
How often the required tests change.
research_questions: Who issues the certification, and is a paper original required?
How often do the required tests change?

already_counted.description: Passing the required tests stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No course is rewritten; the file uses the issued certificate

time_saved_range_pct.basis: The conservative case keeps learning and the test in full. The low end moves only the filing of a certificate that already exists. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Judge whether an emergency is in the service area.

steps.what: Observe alarm registers as they sound.
Scan maps of the dispatch service area.
Determine whether this emergency is in the dispatch service area.
Note the determination the dispatcher made.

tasks.design: The dispatcher observes the alarm and scans the map. The dispatcher determines whether that emergency is inside the service area. A note records the determination. No boundary tool makes the determination.
tasks.previous_blocker: The alarm register and the map were already watched by the dispatcher, because a point near the boundary is a judgement.
tasks.enabler_now: The existing map can be opened to the alarm. The determination stays the dispatcher's.
tasks.still_hard: Boundaries follow roads and agreements, and an alarm coordinate can be off.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher determines whether the emergency is in the service area.
tasks.altitude: Watching the register and determining the area stay with the dispatcher. Scanning the map is a little shorter to open.

reach.task: Take an emergency outside this area
reach.learn: The handoff follows the dispatcher's determination

evidence.claim: The existing map can be opened to an alarm. Whether the emergency is in the service area stays the dispatcher's determination.

assumptions: The workflow starts when an alarm sounds and ends when the dispatcher has determined the area. Dispatching a unit stays in its own task.
The note fields are alarm id and inside or outside, written by the dispatcher. A coordinate with no determination is not treated as inside.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree.
Upkeep is keeping the service-area outline the desk already uses. No new outline is drawn by a model.
unknowns: Whether the service-area outline on the map is current.
Who confirms a boundary alarm when the map and the agreement disagree.
research_questions: Is the service-area outline on the map current?
Who confirms an alarm that sits on the boundary?

already_counted.description: Determining the service area stays in full inside that step

incremental.description: No new outline; the desk uses the map it already has

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the map is no faster to open, the low end is the observation and the determination, which stay in full. No tool decides the boundary in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Keep roster and emergency call-out files.

steps.what: Read personnel rosters and pager files.
Update information relating to emergency calls.
Check call-out names against the roster.
Review the files before they are stored.
Maintain files by writing the accepted version.

tasks.design: The dispatcher reads the personnel roster and pager file, updates a name a supervisor has confirmed, and checks the call-out list. {DOCS} writes only the version the dispatcher reviewed. Nobody is paged by this task, and nobody is scored.
tasks.previous_blocker: The same names were kept in two files and copied across by hand.
tasks.enabler_now: One file can hold the roster and the call-out list once a person has accepted the names.
tasks.still_hard: A name can be wrong for the night, and paging someone is a separate decision that stays on the radio.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher checks the names. A stored file does not call anyone out.
tasks.altitude: Copying an accepted roster takes less time. Choosing and checking the names stay with the dispatcher. No page is sent from the file.

reach.learn: The file changes only after that confirmation and the dispatcher's review

evidence.claim: A roster file can be written from names the dispatcher has checked.
The file is a list of names for emergency calls. It does not score anyone and it does not send a page.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a name must change and ends when the accepted file is stored. Paging a person stays on the radio, outside this task.
The fields are name, role, and call-out order. The dispatcher produces the change after a supervisor has confirmed the name. A name with no acceptance is not written. No trait is stored.
The prior treats the task as automate. The steps agree that the copy can be a write, and they keep the name change and the check with the dispatcher.
Upkeep is keeping role labels on the file. No paging rule is added.
unknowns: Who may confirm a name change before the dispatcher writes it.
Whether pager numbers are still in this file or on a separate system.
research_questions: Who confirms a roster change before it is written?
Are pager numbers in this file?

already_counted.description: Reviewing the files stays partly in that step

incremental.description: Keep role labels on the roster file

approvals.approved_version: roster and call-out file the dispatcher reviewed after checking the names

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If the service still keeps a paper call-out card, the write is unused and the low end is the reading and the name check, which stay. No page is sent in either case. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Test alarm systems and report malfunctions.

steps.what: Adjust alarm systems that failed the test.
Report malfunctions found during the test.
Send the malfunction report the dispatcher accepted.

tasks.design: The dispatcher tests and adjusts the communication and alarm equipment. They write the malfunction report from what the test showed. The report is sent only after that. The test is not skipped, and a fault is not invented from a log.
tasks.previous_blocker: The test was hands-on, and the same fault was then telephoned and written.
tasks.enabler_now: A report the dispatcher has written after the test can be sent without a second call, when maintenance accepts a written report.
tasks.still_hard: A test can require a person at the panel, and a fault can be intermittent.
tasks.human_edge: The dispatcher tests the system and writes what failed. A send is not the test.
tasks.altitude: Testing and adjusting stay. Sending a report the dispatcher has already written is shorter when maintenance can read it.

reach.learn: Act on the report the dispatcher wrote after the test

evidence.claim: A malfunction report written after a test can be sent to maintenance.

assumptions: The workflow starts when a test is due and ends when the accepted report is sent. The test and the adjustment stay in person and come before the report.
The report fields are system, what failed, and what the dispatcher adjusted. The dispatcher writes them from the test. A report is not sent for a test that has not happened.
The prior treats the task as human. The steps agree on the test. Only the send of the written report is a message.
Upkeep is keeping the maintenance contact.
unknowns: Whether maintenance still requires a phone call as well as a report.
Which systems the dispatcher tests, and which a technician tests.
research_questions: Does maintenance accept a written report without a phone call?
Which systems does the dispatcher test?

already_counted.description: Testing the systems stays in full inside that step

approvals.approved_version: malfunction report the dispatcher wrote after testing the system

time_saved_range_pct.basis: If maintenance still requires a phone call, the send is unused and the low end is the test, the adjustment, and the call, which stay. The report is never sent before the test. Provisional, not a measured result.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Certification tests, the service-area determination, and testing the alarms stay with the dispatcher. An accepted roster file can be stored without a second copy. The file does not page anyone and does not score them.
reach: Maintenance receives a malfunction report written after the test
A supervisor sees a roster version the dispatcher reviewed
skills_to_grow: Determining the service area without a boundary tool
Checking call-out names before the file is stored
Writing a fault report only after the test
role.ambitious_version: The roster is the version the dispatcher checked, and a fault report exists only because they tested the system.
